title: Annual spectral templates increase later error for the known 0.88-day signal near KIC 8462852 in Kepler Q10 to Q17
abstract: We test whether the known 0.88-day spectral structure near KIC 8462852 repeats with the annual Kepler detector cycle. We fit spectral templates in release 25 quarters 2 to 9 and predict quarters 10 to 17. A one-harmonic fit with a five-day baseline gives 6.11 percent more later error in raw aperture flux and 4.86 percent more in corrected flux than a template that ignores season. Removal of the two shortest later quarters retains negative gains. A three-harmonic fit gives a small 1.52 percent gain. A strong planted annual signal gives a 66.77 percent gain. The tested annual model does not give a stable prediction gain. Low signal strength, unequal coverage, aperture changes and correlated noise limit this result. The products share exposures. No independent telescope or source pixels are tested. No new source or planet is found. Code, aggregate profiles, figures, exact input hashes and separate-scratch reproduction steps are included.

display.caption: Normalized fitted-score profiles across four detector cycles. The cyan line separates early fits from later tests. Short quarters and grid boundaries limit peak interpretation.
